journey.title: Tab away after typing an unavailable delivery date
journey.goal: Leaving the date field with Tab closes the calendar even when the typed date is outside the delivery window

steps.title: Type a date outside the delivery window

functionalJourney.title: Move the delivery into June with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Clicking through the calendar to June and choosing a day fills the delivery date

guards.title: Type a valid delivery date and Tab away
guards.goal: A correctly typed date is committed and the calendar closes when the user tabs away

plan.root_cause: The datepicker does not hide when the input loses focus (e.g., on Tab) if the entered date is invalid, because the setDate method returns early without triggering the hide via autohide.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a blur event listener to the input field in non-inline mode that calls the datepicker's hide method, ensuring the picker is hidden and edit mode is exited when the input loses focus, regardless of date validity.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: The datepicker will now close when the input loses focus (e.g., via Tab key) even if the entered date is outside the valid range, ensuring that keyboard users can move focus away from the date field without the datepicker remaining open and potentially trapping focus or obscuring other content.
functional_risks: Hiding the picker on blur might interfere with legitimate use cases where the user expects the picker to remain open while interacting with other page elements, though this is not a typical interaction pattern for date pickers.

The blur listener may cause the picker to hide prematurely if the input programmatically loses focus without the user intending to leave the field, though such scenarios are rare and the hide method is safe to call multiple times.
verification_requirements: Verify that typing an invalid date (outside the minDate/maxDate range) and pressing Tab results in the datepicker closing and focus moving to the next element.
Verify that typing a valid date (within the minDate/maxDate range) and pressing Tab still results in the datepicker closing and focus moving to the next element (ensuring no regression).
Verify that the datepicker still functions correctly for mouse interactions (e.g., clicking a date in the picker updates the input and closes the picker).
Verify that inline datepickers are not affected by this change.
